text:
B: Hello? Oh, hello, can you see me alright? Sorry, I wasn't sure which button.
A: Yes, you're fine, I can see you. I'm Claire.
B: Julie. Hello, Claire. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous with these video things, my son normally sets it up for me.
A: Don't worry, I nearly joined with my camera pointing at the ceiling. Where are you?
B: Basingstoke. I'm in the kitchen, you can probably see the fridge behind me, it's a bit of a state.
A: Ha, it's nowhere near as bad as mine. I'm in Faversham, in Kent.
B: Oh, lovely. Is that by the sea?
A: Sort of. It's on a creek, and there are marshes, and then the sea's a bit further out. I walk the dog out there most mornings. He rolls in anything dead, so it's not as idyllic as it sounds.
B: Oh, I saw the dog lead in your picture! I've got one too, Pip, Jack Russell cross. He's going grey round the muzzle now, bless him.
A: Mine's a terrier as well, Moss. Elderly and appallingly behaved. Is yours well behaved?
B: Erm, mostly. He barks at the postman. What do you do, Claire, if you don't mind me asking?
A: I've got an interior design studio in Canterbury with a business partner. I do the clients and the ideas, she does everything sensible. What about you?
B: I'm a care assistant, senior care assistant, at a care home. Older people, a lot of them with dementia. I've been doing it, oh, since my early forties. I came to it late, really.
A: How did you come to it?
B: Erm, well, I looked after my mum. She had dementia, and after she went I sort of thought, well, I know how to do this now, do you know what I mean? And I didn't want to go back to shop work. So I did my NVQs and that was that. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for a first chat.
A: No, not at all, that's a much better answer than most people give. It must be hard, though. Do you get attached?
B: Oh, terribly. You're not supposed to, but you do. There was one lady who used to call me "my Julie". When she passed I sat in the car park and cried my eyes out. The managers always say you get used to it, but you don't really.
A: No, I don't think you should get used to it, honestly. I'd worry about the ones who did.
B: That's what I think! Some of the agency staff, they just... anyway. Sorry, I've gone off on one.
A: You haven't. Are you working today?
B: I was on an early, so I'm absolutely shattered. I'll be asleep in front of Strictly by eight.
A: I don't watch it, I'm afraid. My daughter does, she's eleven, she does all the scoring with a little notepad.
B: Oh, bless her. That's what my granddaughter does! Has she got a favourite?
A: Probably. I'd be lying if I said I knew who it was.
B: [laughs] Well, you'll have to ask her and tell me. Is that... sorry, is that a painting behind you? It's very big.
A: It is. It's one of mine, actually. Half-finished, and crooked, as you can see. I keep meaning to—
